## Replication in linguistics

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
> \[O\]nly **1 in 1,250** experimental linguistic articles contains an independent direct replication.

> The observed smaller number of citations of replication studies compared to corresponding initial studies is also in line with the **lack of perceived value of replication** studies reported in other fields.

--- @kobrock2023
:::

## Statistical power in linguistics

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
> An opportunistic review of seven papers from the November 2017 issue of this journal containing statistical analyses of acoustic speech production data found the **number of participants to range from 11 to 39**.

--- @kirby2018

> In group differences research, the **median sample sizes** (n = 18 and n = 14 for case and control groups, respectively) were **insufficient** for detecting large, medium, or small effect sizes.

--- @gaeta2020

> \[O\]f the 1004 studies reviewed by Lehtonen et al. (2018) 878 had sample sizes **smaller than 50 participants per group** (i.e., 87%) and 987 had sample sizes smaller than 100 (98%).

--- @brysbaert2020
:::

## Reproducibility in linguistics

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
> 35% of the articles were published open access and the rates of **sharing materials, data, and protocols were below 10%**.
> None of the articles reported preregistrations, 1% reported replications, and 10% had conflict of interest statements.
> These rates have not increased noticeably between 2008/2009 and 2018/2019.

--- @bochynska2023
:::

## How to write an RR

::: callout-tip
## Stage 1 manuscript

-   Write **introduction, background and methods**.

-   Target **specific and clear** RQs (and RHs) and assess **feasibility** (within constraints).

-   **Pilot** studies or data **simulations**.

-   Prepare a **research compendium** and ensure **reproducibility**.
:::

. . .

::: callout-important
## In Principle Acceptance

Carry out the study according to the Stage 1 registered protocol.
:::

. . .

::: callout-tip
## Stage 2 manuscript

-   Write **results** (of registered analyses + optional exploratory non-registered analyses), **discussion** and **conclusion**.
:::

## Venues

-   Registered Reports in Linguistics (RRLing): <https://journals.ed.ac.uk/rrling/index>

-   Journal of Phonetics.

-   Bilingualism: Language and Cognition.

-   Glossa Psycholinguistics.
:::

## Guidance for supervisors

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
-   **PhD students** especially can benefit from RRs.

-   **Master students**: Stage 1 manuscript as dissertation.

    -   Start very early (Semester 1).

    -   Arrangements for post-IPA.
:::
